_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Kyrgyzstan covering Scythian/Saka burials, Turkic khaganates, Karakhanid Islamisation, Mongol conquest, Kyrgyz ethnogenesis, Kokand Khanate dominance, Russian conquest 1876, Basmachi resistance, Soviet Kirghizia (cotton, literacy), 1990 Osh riots, independence 1991, Tulip Revolution 2005, April Revolution 2010, ethnic clashes (Osh 2010), constitutional shifts, and Manas epic heritage.

religion.note: Nomadic Kyrgyz Islam blended with Tengrism/shamanic traditions; growing conservative Islam; secular constitution

ethnic_groups.name: Kyrgyz
ethnic_groups.notes: Turkic; 40 tribes reflected on national flag (40-ray sun); nomadic pastoralist heritage; Manas epic (500,000+ lines); north-south clan divide; yurt culture

ethnic_groups.name: Uzbek
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern Kyrgyzstan (Osh, Jalal-Abad); settled/farming; 2010 ethnic violence killed ~470; tension over representation; distinct from northern-dominated politics

ethnic_groups.name: Russian
ethnic_groups.notes: Declining (was 21% in 1989); Bishkek/Chuy; Soviet settlers; educated professionals; many emigrated

ethnic_groups.name: Dungan (Chinese Hui Muslim)
ethnic_groups.notes: Fled China 1877-1878; Karakol area; speak Gansu Mandarin in Cyrillic; farming; unique cuisine

ethnic_groups.name: Uyghur
ethnic_groups.notes: Turkic; trade; Bishkek/Tokmok; Chinese border areas

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Tajik, Tatar, Ukrainian, Korean, German)
ethnic_groups.notes: Tajik minority in south; Soviet-era deportee communities; small but culturally distinct

country_profile.notes_unique: Only Central Asian country to have had two successful revolutions (2005, 2010); 'Switzerland of Central Asia' (mountainous, 94% above 1000m); Issyk-Kul (world's second-largest alpine lake); Epic of Manas (UNESCO intangible heritage); nomadic games (kok-boru/buzkashi)

trade.notes: Large trade deficit offset by remittances; Kumtor gold mine major export; Dordoi/Kara-Suu bazaars re-export hubs; post-2022 Russian goods re-export boom.

infrastructure.notes: Mountain terrain limits transport; China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway proposed; Bishkek-Osh road vital; hydropower exports potential; winter energy shortages despite capacity.

governance_indices.notes: Historically most democratic Central Asian state; post-2020 revolution authoritarian turn under Japarov; presidential system restored; civil society relatively active.

geography.terrain: 90%+ mountainous; Tien Shan and Pamir-Alay ranges; Fergana Valley edge; alpine meadows and glaciers
geography.notes: Central Asian mountain republic; Issyk-Kul world's second-largest high-altitude lake; glacial meltwater critical for region; nomadic herding heritage; complex Fergana Valley borders.

economy_extended.notes: Remittance-dependent (30%+ GDP from Russia-based workers); gold mining (Kumtor mine); hydropower potential; informal/grey economy large; post-2022 Russian sanctions evasion transit.

health.notes: Soviet-era infrastructure degrading; high TB rates; rural healthcare access limited; high altitude health challenges; mandatory health insurance system.

food_agriculture.notes: Mountain agriculture; nomadic pastoral heritage; walnut forests unique globally; dairy/meat processing growing; water-rich but inefficient irrigation.

security_stability.internal_conflicts: Fergana Valley ethnic tensions; periodic political instability
security_stability.notes: Only Central Asian democracy (contested); 2005, 2010, 2020 revolutions; Fergana Valley inter-ethnic violence 2010; Kyrgyz-Tajik border clashes; CSTO member.

environment_climate.notes: Glacial retreat threatening water supply for Central Asia; hydropower dominant (90%); walnut-fruit forests biodiversity hotspot; earthquake-prone; uranium tailings legacy.

demographics_extended.notes: Young, growing population; massive labor migration to Russia; Kyrgyz 73%, Uzbek 15%; north-south regional divide; bride kidnapping traditions persisting.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Mountainous Central Asian republic; most democratic in region; remittance-dependent economy.

music_art_traditions: Epic of Manas (world's longest epic poem)
cultural_heritage.notes: Nomadic Turkic heritage; Epic of Manas cultural pillar; World Nomad Games host; yurt-dwelling tradition.

energy.notes: Hydropower-dominant (Toktogul Dam); water-energy nexus disputes with Uzbekistan; imports gas and oil; Kambarata HPP planned.

human_rights_gender.notes: Bride kidnapping (ala kachuu) persists despite ban; 2020/2021 revolutions; ethnic tensions (Uzbek minority in south); democratic backsliding under Japarov.

legal_system.notes: 2021 constitution expanded presidential powers; Supreme Court; Constitutional Chamber; local courts – Aksakal (elder) mediation.

tourism.notes: Adventure/eco-tourism growing; CBT (Community Based Tourism) model; horse trekking; yurt stays; Silk Road heritage.

transport.notes: Mountain terrain limits infrastructure; no continuous railway; dependent on marshrutkas; China–Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan railway proposed.

current_leader.name: Sadyr Japarov
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Came to power after October 2020 protests; was imprisoned for hostage-taking; populist; pushed new constitution (2021) expanding presidential powers; nationalist; Kumtor gold mine nationalisation

former_leaders.name: Sooronbay Jeenbekov
former_leaders.notes: Resigned after post-election protests October 2020; southern Kyrgyz

former_leaders.name: Almazbek Atambayev
former_leaders.notes: First peaceful transfer; later arrested on corruption charges; stormed by security forces 2019; sentenced then freed then re-arrested

former_leaders.name: Roza Otunbayeva
former_leaders.notes: Transitional president after April Revolution; Central Asia's first female head of state; oversaw new parliamentary constitution

former_leaders.name: Kurmanbek Bakiyev
former_leaders.notes: Tulip Revolution brought to power; became authoritarian; family corruption; overthrown April 2010; fled to Belarus

former_leaders.name: Askar Akayev
former_leaders.notes: Physicist; initially democratic reformer ('island of democracy'); became authoritarian; overthrown in Tulip Revolution; fled to Russia

920.description: The emergence of a distinct Kyrgyz tribal society in the Tian Shan, the oral epic Manas, conflicts with the Dzungar Mongols and the Kokand Khanate, and the formation of tribal wings (kanat).

sub_clusters.name: Epic of Manas and Tribal Identity
sub_clusters.description: The crystallization of Kyrgyz identity around the oral Epic of Manas — one of the world's longest epic poems — the tribal structure of left (sol) and right (ong) wings, and mountain nomadic culture.
key_events: The Epic of Manas — 500,000 lines, the longest oral epic in the world — transmitted through generations of manaschi bards

sub_clusters.name: Kokand Fortresses and Kyrgyz Resistance
